reviewed_existing_core.finding: The existing cooldown is anchored on the last emitted notification. Grouped and budget-rejected raw triggers do not advance that anchor. Therefore changing budget admission changes subsequent grouped candidate streams.

window_revision_before_new_outcomes.superseded_proposal: Separate Euler March2023 and Beanstalk April2022 thirty-day windows.
window_revision_before_new_outcomes.reason: A shared Ethereum source partition can be scanned once per date for both predeclared emitters, reducing acquisition time and temporary-storage cost.
window_revision_before_new_outcomes.selection_disclosure: The window ends after the already-known Beanstalk incident day. Selection is label-informed and resource-motivated, not a random background sample or an independent incident holdout. Euler March13 remains previously observed development/supplementary evidence.
window_revision_before_new_outcomes.required_before_execution: Freeze exact historical emitter addresses and evidence that they were deployed/relevant throughout the proposed period. An inactive emitter remains a reported zero/low-activity population; do not replace dates or addresses after seeing policy outcomes.
window_revision_before_new_outcomes.completeness: All thirty source dates, including zero-selected-log dates, must have enumerated complete source partitions and validation status. Missing partitions make the primary run incomplete; do not silently join across gaps or shorten the window after outcomes.

common_stream_contract.clock: t is original event_time_ns in integer POSIX nanoseconds, in canonical block/transaction/log order. UTC day is floor(t/T), with T=86400000000000. Do not replace this clock with replay speed, CPU-dependent completion time or first-event-relative time.
common_stream_contract.causality_scope: Prefix-causal historical logical-time simulation. The experiment does not establish when source logs/features were observed operationally, nor live notification latency.
common_stream_contract.detector: All accepted logs from the predeclared emitter; count in (t-60 seconds,t], including current; raw trigger iff count>=10.
common_stream_contract.grouping: A raw trigger is a candidate iff no prior emission exists or t-last_emitted_ns>=300000000000. Grouped and rejected rows do not extend cooldown. Only actual emission changes last_emitted_ns.
common_stream_contract.initial_state: At the exact window start: empty rolling log history, no prior emitted notification, empty seen-ID state, zero daily emitted counts; token bucket full once. This is an explicit cold-start experiment, not an unobserved pre-window steady state.
common_stream_contract.continuous_state: Do not reset rolling feature history, watermark, deduplication identities, grouping anchor or token credit at file/UTC-day boundaries. Grouping across midnight remains active.
common_stream_contract.budget_scope: Recommended primary contract: independent B=5 per emitter per UTC day per policy. Two emitters can therefore produce up to ten combined notifications per day. A shared cross-emitter budget would be a different study and must not be substituted silently.
common_stream_contract.rejected_candidates: Discard immediately; do not buffer, replay at credit release, or emit automatically when time passes without a new eligible event.
common_stream_contract.invalid_duplicate_late: Rejected duplicate, conflicting or late deliveries cannot refill/reset/consume an allocator or alter grouping. A decreasing accepted logical timestamp fails before mutation.

greedy.reset: Only the daily emitted count changes with UTC day.

paced_cumulative_quota.released_quota: q(t)=min(5,1+(5*(t mod T))//T), using integer arithmetic.
paced_cumulative_quota.carry: Unused released quota accumulates within the current UTC day. It expires at midnight; the new day begins with one released unit. A late first event sees all units released earlier that day.
paced_cumulative_quota.interpretation: This constrains cumulative expenditure, not the minimum spacing between emissions. After inactivity, several emissions can occur subject to the unchanged 300-second cooldown.

token_bucket_capacity_one.representation: Integer credit in [0,T], where T credit units equal one token. Capacity=T, refill adds five credit units per elapsed nanosecond.
token_bucket_capacity_one.initialization: credit=T and last_refill_ns=window_start_ns, exactly once at experiment start.
token_bucket_capacity_one.refill: For each accepted event at t: credit=min(T,credit+5*(t-last_refill_ns)); last_refill_ns=t. This may be calculated before grouping; spending still requires a candidate.
token_bucket_capacity_one.admit: candidate and credit==T and emitted_on_current_utc_day<5; on emission subtract T and increment the current-day emitted count.
token_bucket_capacity_one.midnight: Carry credit and last_refill_ns continuously. Reset only the daily emitted count; do not refill a token just because UTC midnight passed.
token_bucket_capacity_one.rejection: A grouped row or quota/cap rejection consumes no credit. Natural time refill is retained. No deferred emission follows.
token_bucket_capacity_one.implied_spacing: Any two emissions must be at least T/5=17280000000000 ns (4h48m) apart, including across midnight. With capacity one and this refill rate the explicit five-per-UTC-day cap is defensive/redundant for a correct monotone implementation; retain and test it.

grouping_fairness_and_attribution.primary_comparison: End-to-end detector/grouping/admission policy comparison: every policy gets identical accepted input events and identical raw scores, but its own last-notified grouping state and allocator state.
required_invariants: Identical accepted-event identities and scores across all three policies
Policy-specific candidate, grouped, quota-rejected, daily-cap-rejected and emitted counts reconcile exactly
grouping_fairness_and_attribution.invalid_analysis: Do not describe the primary run as three allocators applied to an identical pregrouped candidate stream. Do not interpret a lower rejection fraction over each policy's different candidate denominator as isolated allocation efficiency.
grouping_fairness_and_attribution.recommended_secondary_crosscheck: Freeze a shadow policy-independent reference stream before outcomes: after every raw trigger at least300s after the previous reference candidate, emit a reference candidate and advance the reference anchor regardless of any budget decision. Feed those same candidates to each allocator without policy-dependent regrouping. Report this separately as an allocation-only diagnostic, not as the unchanged primary grouping contract.
grouping_fairness_and_attribution.if_secondary_omitted: The primary workload comparison remains valid, but attribute results to coupled grouping plus allocation and make no isolated-budget-mechanism claim.

metrics_to_freeze: Per emitter, policy and UTC day: accepted logs, raw triggers, grouped rows, candidates, quota rejections, hard-day-cap rejections, emitted notifications, unused daily capacity and fraction of all raw triggers emitted.
Include all thirty dates in totals and daily distributions; show zero-log days explicitly. Report active-day summaries only as separately labelled supplementary quantities.

First/last emission UTC time, time of fifth emission when present, inter-emission gaps across the entire continuous window, and a fixed 24-bin UTC hour histogram. These are allocation/workload descriptions, not attack-detection quality.

For pre-frozen source transaction memberships, report matching selected logs and their raw/grouped/rejected/emitted statuses, alongside budget/credit immediately before the earliest reported execution. Missing membership or no emission must be explicit, not converted to a false-negative or recall estimate.

Distinguish event-time allocation timestamps from measured local processing costs. If feature computation is shared across policies, do not present allocation-only timings as three separately measured end-to-end detector pipelines.
essential_tests: Paced: one nanosecond before, exactly at, and after all five release boundaries; late first event; unused within-day carry and midnight expiry.
Token: full initial token exactly once; rejection at17280s-1ns; admission exactly at17280s; fractional credit retained; long inactivity never accumulates more than one token.
Midnight: last emission shortly before midnight cannot receive a fresh bucket token at midnight; daily counts reset but rolling count and300s grouping anchor do not.
Same-timestamp events use exact canonical order; an allocator-only cooldown0 fixture tests quota arithmetic, while integration fixtures retain cooldown300s.
A rejected candidate is never emitted later without a new event; rejected/grouped records never advance last_emitted or spend quota. Exact duplicate and late replay cannot change any policy state.
A synthetic prefix where greedy emits and paced rejects must produce the expected different subsequent grouping eligibility; the common raw stream must remain identical.

Prefix invariance under arbitrary appended future inputs; chunk/file partition invariance; checkpoint round-trip equivalence including credit, last_refill_ns, UTC counts, rolling state, identities and grouping anchor.
Long gaps and zero-selected-log days; all thirty midnight crossings; strict nondecreasing logical time; per-day emission count<=5, paced emitted<=released quota, and token inter-emission gap>=17280s.
Different replay speed and injected CPU/write delays cannot change semantic policy decisions because allocation uses the fixed source-time clock.

Persist policy/config hashes and policy-namespaced notification IDs. If the durable wrapper is extended, include all new allocator fields in atomic state/outbox checkpoints and repeat its meaningful crash-boundary tests.
remaining_prefreeze_gates: No blocking design definition remains for freezing this configuration and starting complete-window acquisition.

The implementation must pass the listed exact-boundary, causal-prefix and state-continuity checks before policy comparisons. Rejection-reason precedence should be deterministic: grouped before allocation; hard daily cap before quota/token shortage.

Historical deployment/population attribution is being verified separately; a historical source code snapshot alone is not proof of deployed facets/ABI. This does not require changing the declared all-topic fixed-address workload or adding receipt/semantic decoding.
Freeze executed implementation, complete inventory/input hashes and the existing label manifest before replay; preserve the stated scope and report every planned cell.
blocked_claims: Pacing was independently validated by rescuing the already-observed Euler incident.
The two emitters or thirty days provide thirty independent attack trials.
Unknown background transactions are negative labels, or source transaction membership provides complete incident recall.
Compressed playback preserves a daily budget when the allocator uses playback UTC day.
All three primary policies had an identical grouped candidate stream.
execution_performed_in_this_review: Read-only design/config/source review and epoch/cell-count checks; no new payload acquisition, policy outcome comparison, model fit, tuning, main implementation edit or GitHub write.
